# cmd_new in scripts/zenodo.py). Everything else is yours to replace.
#
# The file renders as-is: the worked example below is a complete miniature
# report. Render once to confirm the toolchain, then write over it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

title: "Audit of Author et al. (YEAR)"        # how the report is cited
subtitle: "One line saying what was audited"  # shown under the title

ace-id: "ACE2026000"

date: "2026-06-21"

# Written by a LIVE `zenodo.py deposit`; leave empty until then.
doi: ""
concept-doi: ""

# DOIs of the papers this report audits -> Zenodo relation "reviews". This is
# what links the audit to the audited work in the DataCite graph, so check every
# digit; `deposit` resolves each one against Crossref and prints the title.
audited: []
# DOIs of supporting literature -> Zenodo relation "references". Everything
# cited in the body is picked up automatically from references.bib; this is for
# anything else worth linking.
cites: []

# Citation counts for the Impact section, written by

# Uncomment after the first run.

#   spread-guidelines: 0
#   retrieved: "YYYY-MM-DD"

# verdict. Aim for 160 characters. See scripts/README.md for the formula.
description: "One-sentence summary of the audit finding and recommendation."
# Optional per-report preview image, 1200x630, relative to this folder:
# image: images/social.png

# What this report audits, in four facets. `categories:` is written from these

population: ["Heart Disease"]

abstract: "What was audited, what the audit found, how many instances of Research Integrity Violations across how many categories, and what editorial action is recommended."

<!-- ===========================================================
     HOW TO WRITE AN ACE REPORT
     ===========================================================

     RIV LABELS. Refer to a violation as @riv-X.Y. It renders as the bold,
     linked label "Category Name (RIV X.Y)", with the name read from riv.yml so
     it can never be misspelled or drift. [-@riv-X.Y] gives the compact
     "RIV X.Y". An unknown number stops the render.

     DECLARING INSTANCES. Put the count in front of the reference at the place
     the finding is documented, written as one token: N-@riv-1.7, where N is
     the number of instances. The count and hyphen are stripped from the
     rendered page, so the sentence can be worded any way you like, and every
     later plain @riv-1.7 is only a link. See the worked finding below for a
     real one. (N is a letter here on purpose: an actual digit would itself be
     counted, because the summary table reads this file as text and does not
     skip comments.) Declarations
     of the same RIV in different sections add up. The unit of counting is on
     riv.qmd under "Counting" (per article for 1.3 and 3.3, per impossible
     statistic for 2.2, and so on).

     CRITERIA. Every RIV on riv.qmd lists lettered criteria that must each be
     met. A finding section should make plain how the record satisfies them,
     in prose, not by quoting the taxonomy back at the reader.

     SECTION LABELS. Give every finding section a {#sec-...} label. The summary
     table links each RIV back to the sections that declared it.

     TAXONOMY VERSION. State it once, where the first finding section begins.

     TABLE NOTES. Start a note with "Note." and the helpers render the label in
     italic grey, flush left, in both HTML and PDF.

     BEFORE PUBLISHING.
       python3 scripts/citations.py reports/ACE2026000/index.qmd   # impact
       python3 scripts/riv_check.py                                # labels, counts
       quarto render
     =========================================================== -->


## Executive summary

### Description of audited studies

What the audited articles claim to report: design, population, intervention,
outcome measure, and timing. Enough for a reader to follow every later finding
without opening the originals.

### Impact of audited studies

Run `python3 scripts/citations.py reports/ACE2026000/index.qmd` first: it
writes `data/citations.csv` and the `impact:` block in the front matter. Then
delete the two `eval`/`include` lines from each chunk below to switch them on,
and write the paragraph between them using inline R, like this:

```
Based on OpenAlex (retrieved INLINE(impact$retrieved)), the audited studies are
cited by INLINE(impact$cited) articles in total, INLINE(impact$reviews) of which
are meta-analyses or reviews (see @tbl-impact).
```

where `INLINE(x)` is a backtick, the letter r, a space, `x`, and a closing
backtick. A work that cites an audited study is described as *infected*: its
findings incorporate results this report identifies as unreliable.

```{r}
#| label: impact-numbers
#| eval: false
#| include: false
cites <- read.csv("reports/ACE2026000/data/citations.csv")
impact <- list(
  cited     = sum(cites$total),
  reviews   = sum(cites$reviews),
  retrieved = cites$retrieved[1]
)
```

```{r}
#| label: impact-table
#| eval: false
#| include: false
#| results: asis
cites <- citation_table(
  "reports/ACE2026000/data/citations.csv",
  labels = c("10.xxxx/yyyy" = "@citekey"),
  caption = "Citation counts for audited studies",
  label = "tbl-impact"
)
```


## Findings

Findings in this report are labeled using version 1.0 of the [ACE Research
Integrity Violations taxonomy (ACE-RIV)](https://auditclinicalevidence.org/riv.html).

### A finding, named for what was found {#sec-example-finding}

State the observation first, in plain terms, and show where it comes from: the
table, figure, registration entry, or metadata field a reader can check for
themselves. Reproduce only what the point requires.

Then show that the record meets each criterion of the category. For
@riv-2.2 that means the reported values are arithmetically impossible for the
stated sample size, and that the impossibility does not depend on an assumption
the article leaves open. Three of the reported means and standard deviations
fail that test, which warrants three instances of 3-@riv-2.2.

Close by saying what the finding does and does not establish. A finding under a
category means the record contains evidence matching that category, not that ACE
has determined why the evidence exists.

```{r}
#| label: fig-example
#| fig-cap: "Delete this chunk. It exists to show the house figure style."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5

dat <- tibble(
  x = rep(seq(0, 10, length.out = 40), 2),
  group = rep(c("Group A", "Group B"), each = 40),
  y = case_when(
    group == "Group A" ~ 2.5 + 0.55 * x + rnorm(40, 0, 0.8),
    group == "Group B" ~ 1.5 + 0.95 * x + rnorm(40, 0, 0.8)
  )
)

ggplot(dat, aes(x = x, y = y, color = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", linewidth = 1.15, alpha = 0.16) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Group A" = ace_blue, "Group B" = ace_purple)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Group A" = ace_blue, "Group B" = ace_purple)) +
  labs(
    title = "Example Regression Figure",
    subtitle = "Two fitted lines with semi-transparent confidence bands",
    x = "Predictor",
    y = "Outcome",
    caption = "Note. Simulated data shown for ACE figure style development."
  ) +
  theme_ace()
```

### A second finding {#sec-second-finding}

One section per finding. Where two findings share evidence, say so and link the
earlier section with @sec-example-finding rather than repeating it.


## Conclusion {#sec-conclusion}

Summarize what the audit established, in the order it matters. Then state the
recommendation, and say plainly that it is the authors' professional opinion
based on the evidence set out above: correction, expression of concern,
retraction, or no action warranted.

<!-- Generated from the "N-@riv-X.Y" declarations above; the render stops on a
     number that is not in riv.yml, and on a report with no declarations. -->

```{r}
#| label: riv-summary
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
riv <- riv_summary_table("reports/ACE2026000/index.qmd",
  caption = "Summary of Research Integrity Violations identified across the audited studies",
  label = "tbl-riv-summary")
```
